items.settingsPath: Install Outlook from the Microsoft Store. Mail and Calendar have been discontinued by Microsoft.
items.name: Mail and Calendar
items.desc: Discontinued by Microsoft; kept only for legacy accounts.

items.settingsPath: Install Outlook from the Microsoft Store, and undo the run to unblock the updater channel.
items.name: New Outlook for Windows
items.desc: The web-wrapper mail client Microsoft pushes hard. Also blocks the separate Windows Update channel that reinstalls it.

items.settingsPath: Install Microsoft Teams from teams.microsoft.com or the Store.
items.name: Microsoft Teams (personal)
items.desc: The free consumer client. Work Teams deployed by an organization is left alone.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall the Microsoft 365 app from the Store.
items.name: Microsoft 365 hub tile
items.desc: The Office upsell shortcut, not Office itself.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Media Player from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Media Player
items.desc: The built-in music and audio player.
items.riskNote: It is the default audio player. Removing it means audio files have no handler until you set another.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Movies and TV from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Movies and TV
items.desc: Store video playback.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Phone Link from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Phone Link and Cross Device
items.desc: Also removes the Mobile Devices integration.
items.riskNote: Removes phone integration and the Mobile Devices panel in Settings.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall the People app from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: People app
items.desc: The People contacts app. The shell component behind it is an in-box part of Windows and stays.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Get Help from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Get Help

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Tips from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Tips and Get Started

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Sticky Notes from the Microsoft Store. Notes synced to your account come back with it.
items.name: Sticky Notes
items.desc: The desktop notes app.
items.riskNote: People genuinely use this and notes are stored locally. Check nothing is in it first.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Windows Maps from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Windows Maps
items.desc: Plus the MapsBroker service and its update tasks.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Clock from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Clock and Alarms
items.desc: Alarms, timers, world clock, and focus sessions.
items.riskNote: Includes alarms, timers, and focus sessions, not just a clock.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Sound Recorder from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Sound Recorder
items.desc: The built-in voice recorder.
items.riskNote: The default voice recorder. Nothing else in Windows replaces it.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Feedback Hub from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Feedback Hub

items.settingsPath: Reinstall from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: 3D Builder, Print 3D, and MR Portal
items.desc: All discontinued by Microsoft.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Dev Home from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Dev Home
items.desc: Deprecated by Microsoft.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Microsoft Journal from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Microsoft Journal

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Microsoft To Do from the Store. Your tasks are stored online and come back with it.
items.name: Microsoft To Do
items.desc: Microsoft's task list app.
items.riskNote: Syncs with Outlook tasks. Removing the app does not delete the tasks.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Power Automate from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Power Automate Desktop

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Whiteboard from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Whiteboard

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Quick Assist from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Quick Assist
items.desc: Microsoft's built-in remote assistance tool.
items.riskNote: Removes Microsoft remote assistance. Worth removing on machines used by people who might be talked through a scam, but you lose an easy support route.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Camera from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Camera app
items.desc: The built-in camera app.
items.riskNote: Some webcam setups and third-party apps hand off to the Camera app for capture.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Photos from the Microsoft Store, or right-click a picture, Open with, Choose another app.
items.name: Photos app
items.desc: The built-in photo viewer and editor.
items.riskNote: The default image viewer. Image files will have no handler until you set another.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Paint from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Paint
items.desc: The in-box image editor.
items.riskNote: Nothing else opens .bmp files by default, and Edit with Paint leaves the image right-click menu. Reinstallable from the Store at any time.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Notepad from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Notepad
items.desc: The in-box plain text editor.
items.riskNote: Nothing opens .txt, .log, or .ini files until you set a replacement, and a good deal of software still opens its readme by handing the path to Notepad.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Calculator from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Calculator
items.desc: The in-box calculator.
items.riskNote: The calculator key on keyboards that have one stops doing anything, and so does typing a sum into Start.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Snipping Tool from the Microsoft Store.
items.name: Snipping Tool
items.desc: The in-box screenshot and screen recording tool.
items.riskNote: Win+Shift+S and the Print Screen key both stop capturing - they are handled by this app rather than by the shell - and nothing else on a clean install saves a screenshot to a file.

items.settingsPath: Undo the run. If that does not bring it back, run: wsreset -i from an administrator prompt, or reinstall it with Add-AppxPackage from an elevated PowerShell.
items.name: Microsoft Store
items.desc: The Microsoft Store client.
items.riskNote: Without the Store you cannot install or update Store apps, and reinstalling the Store itself is difficult.

items.settingsPath: Reinstall Microsoft Edge from microsoft.com/edge.
symptoms: you will need an app to open this
items.name: Uninstall Microsoft Edge
items.desc: Uninstalls the Edge browser and blocks its updater from bringing it back. Outside the EEA, Windows refuses to uninstall Edge at all, so this sets the home region to Ireland for the length of the uninstall and puts it straight back. WebView2 Runtime is kept.
items.riskNote: Windows decides whether Edge may be uninstalled at all, from a regional policy file in System32 that Microsoft added for the Digital Markets Act: outside about thirty-five EEA regions the answer is no, and the uninstaller simply refuses - which is why this used to run and change nothing. This run therefore sets your home region to Ireland just long enough to run the uninstaller and sets it back immediately; the change is also written to the rollback script in case the run is interrupted between the two. Your language, keyboard, and formats are untouched - only the Home location field. If Windows still refuses, the item reports that plainly instead of claiming success. WebView2 is kept, so apps that embed a browser still work, but a few Windows surfaces expect Edge and may fall back awkwardly.
